raw_segments.text: At 20 the beauty of both sexes is equal, but the libertinism of man leads him to make the
distinction and superannuated coquettes are commonly of the same opinion, for when they
can no longer inspire love, they pay for the vigor and vivacity of youth. The French who admit more
of mind into their notions of beauty give the preference to women of 30. I mean to say that
they allow women to be in their most perfect state when vivacity gives place to reason,
and to that majestic seriousness of character which marks maturity, or the resting point.
In youth till 20 the body shoots out, till 30 the solids are attaining a degree of density,
and the flexible muscles, growing daily more rigid, give character to the countenance.
That is, they trace the operations of the mind with the iron pen of fate
and tell us not only what powers are within but how they have been employed.
